descriptor: Operating company · reported in CNY · quoted in HKD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

nplRatio.title: Non-performing loan ratio
nplRatio.content:
The NPL ratio is the share of total loans classified as non-performing (generally 90+ days overdue or otherwise unlikely to be repaid in full) under China's five-tier loan classification.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: it has fallen steadily from 1.46% (FY2018) to 1.31% (FY2025), even through the property-sector stress of 2021-2023 -- CCB's loan book skews toward corporate and mortgage lending with lower exposure to the smaller, more leveraged developers that drove peer NPL spikes.

What to watch:

  • Any uptick, since a bank's credit-impairment charge (provisioning) typically follows NPLs with a lag
  • The ratio against disclosed property and local-government financing vehicle exposure, the two sectors most watched in Chinese bank credit quality

capitalRatio.title: Capital adequacy ratios
capitalRatio.content:
The total capital ratio is total regulatory capital (Tier 1 plus Tier 2) divided by risk-weighted assets; CET1 is the highest-quality subset (common equity only). Chinese regulators set CCB's minimum total capital ratio around 11.5-12.5% depending on its G-SIB/D-SIB surcharge.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: both ratios have risen over the period (total capital 17.2% to 19.7%), comfortably above the regulatory minimum and funded mostly through retained earnings given CCB rarely issues new common equity.

What to watch:

  • The gap between total capital and CET1 -- a widening gap means more of the buffer is AT1/Tier 2 instruments rather than core equity
  • Risk-weighted asset growth outpacing capital growth, which compresses the ratio even if the capital base is rising in absolute terms

interestIncome.title: Gross vs net interest income
interestIncome.content:
Gross interest income is total interest earned on loans, investments and interbank placements before any deduction; net interest income subtracts interest expense paid on deposits and borrowings. The gap between the two lines is interest expense -- CCB's funding cost.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: gross interest income grew faster than net interest income through FY2018-FY2023 as rates rose, then both declined in FY2024-FY2025 as China's benchmark rates were cut and NIM compressed from 2.13% to 1.34% over the same stretch -- the funding-cost gap widened even as the asset side repriced down.

What to watch:

  • The two lines converging or diverging faster than loan growth -- that is rate/funding-cost pressure, not volume
  • This chart is FY-only: the underlying disclosure is not broken out at half-year

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Construction Bank Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
